question: Does WooCommerce Subscriptions Work With Elementor Checkout?
metaDescription: Elementor Pro's WooCommerce checkout widget generally supports subscription products, but a few specific fields need checking before launch.
shortAnswer: Generally yes — Elementor Pro's WooCommerce checkout widget builds on top of WooCommerce's own checkout process rather than replacing its logic, so subscription products, recurring totals, and payment gateway fields typically carry through correctly. The parts worth testing specifically are sign-up fee and trial display, and any custom checkout fields added through Elementor that might not account for subscription-specific line items.

bodyHtml:
How It Works

Elementor's WooCommerce widgets, including the checkout widget, are templating layers over WooCommerce's existing checkout logic — they control layout and styling, not the underlying cart/order processing. Since WooCommerce Subscriptions hooks into that same underlying checkout process, a subscription product added to the cart still triggers the correct recurring-total calculation and payment gateway behavior, regardless of which template renders the visible form.

What Actually Needs Testing

  • Sign-up fee and trial messaging display correctly in the Elementor-styled order summary, since custom styling can sometimes hide or misplace line items that a default WooCommerce checkout template shows clearly.
  • Custom checkout fields added through Elementor don't interfere with subscription-specific data WooCommerce Subscriptions needs to process the order correctly.
  • Payment gateway fields render and submit correctly within the Elementor-styled form, particularly for gateways requiring an iframe or a JavaScript-heavy card element (Stripe's card element, for example).
  • Mixed carts (a subscription product alongside a one-time product) display and total correctly, since this scenario has more edge cases than a cart containing only a subscription.

How to Verify It Properly

  1. Place a full test order for a subscription product through the Elementor-built checkout, confirming the recurring total, any sign-up fee, and trial period all display and process correctly.
  2. Test with each payment gateway the store actually offers, not just one, since gateway-specific fields are where checkout customizations most often cause a problem.
  3. Test a mixed cart if the store sells both subscription and one-time products together.
  4. Keep Elementor, Elementor Pro, WooCommerce, and WooCommerce Subscriptions all updated together, since compatibility between page builders and WooCommerce's checkout internals can shift across major updates on either side.

See Elementor customization if the checkout needs adjustments to properly surface subscription-specific details.
